title: Teriyaki Salmon
subtitle: Salmon glazed in soy, mirin, and sake sauce
excerpt: Salmon fillets marinated in a teriyaki sauce of soy, mirin, and sake, then pan-fried and basted until deeply glazed and caramelised. Quick to cook and deeply savoury.

recipe.sourceNotes: Teriyaki is a Japanese cooking technique in which food is grilled or pan-fried and basted repeatedly with a sauce of soy sauce, mirin, and sake (or sugar). The word comes from teri, the shine produced by the sugar and soy glaze, and yaki, the cooking method (grilling or pan-frying). The technique is ancient in Japan but became widely known in the West through Japanese restaurants and supermarket sauces from the 1970s. Salmon teriyaki is not a traditional Japanese dish (salmon was not widely consumed in Japan until the 1980s, when Norwegian salmon was imported successfully), but it is now extremely common both in Japan and internationally.

recipeTools.notes: A non-stick or well-seasoned pan to prevent the glaze from sticking.

content.text: Pat the salmon fillets completely dry before cooking: moisture on the surface prevents good colour. The glaze goes on in the last 2 to 3 minutes of cooking rather than at the start: added too early it will burn before the fish is cooked through. Watch carefully once the glaze is in the pan, as the sugars in the mirin can turn from caramelised to burnt very quickly.

items.preparation: about 180 g each, skin-on, patted dry

content.text: Mix the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar together in a small bowl. Marinate the salmon in this mixture for 10 minutes. Remove from the marinade and pat gently dry. Reserve the marinade.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the salmon skin-side down and cook for 3 to 4 minutes without moving until the skin is crisp. Flip carefully and cook for 2 minutes on the flesh side.

Pour the reserved marinade into the pan around the salmon. Let it bubble and reduce for 1 to 2 minutes, spooning the glaze over the salmon as it cooks, until the sauce has thickened and the salmon is lacquered and glossy.
Serve with steamed rice and pak choi. Scatter with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.
